title: Raga Dhanasri
hookLine: a raga of true wealth that opens with a frightened soul

cards: Who counts as rich? A bank would answer with a number. A grandmother might answer with the people at her table.
Tradition links today's raga with contentment and true wealth, so you might expect its first hymn to sound settled and full. Instead, the first voice you hear in Dhanasri is afraid.
Today: Raga Dhanasri, and how a raga of true wealth starts from fear.

teach.h: FIRST VOICE: MY SOUL IS AFRAID.
teach.b: Dhanasri comes after Sorath in the Granth's order. Its first hymn is Guru Nanak's, and it begins, jeeo darat hai aapna. In paraphrase: my soul is afraid; to whom should I cry out?

teach.h: THE GIVER WHO IS ALWAYS GIVING.
teach.b: Then the hymn answers itself: I serve the one who makes pain forgotten, the giver who is always, always giving. It doesn't pretend the fear isn't there. It names it, then turns toward a giver who never runs out.
Further in, a hymn of Guru Amar Das plays on the raga's name. In paraphrase: Dhanasri is known as truly wealthy when she does the True Guru's work, giving over body and mind to that service.
Dhanvanti, the wealthy one, chimes with Dhanasri, and the Guru lets the two words ring together.
Some readers hear the soul as a bride in her, and if so, the bride's riches aren't jewelry. They're the work she does. Side by side, the two hymns make one idea in two steps.
Fear first, honestly said: I don't have enough, I can't hold this. Then a different wealth: a giver who keeps giving, and a life spent in service.
Contentment follows, because a person held by an endless giver can stop counting.

how: Ragis sing shabads from the Dhanasri section of the Guru Granth Sahib in Raga Dhanasri during kirtan, and the raga's opening hymn by Guru Nanak is sung in gurdwaras as well as read.

games.q: you're opening a raga linked with true wealth. how does Guru Nanak's first hymn begin?
o: with a frightened soul asking whom to cry to.
games.why: it begins with fear, said honestly, then turns to the one who makes pain forgotten, the giver who is always giving.

practice: If you can, play a shabad in Raga Dhanasri, then let one worry about not having enough come up, money, time, strength or patience, and name it plainly, the way the hymn does.
Then slowly count what holds you right now that you didn't earn: breath, a floor, someone who would pick up if you called. If you pray, say Waheguru after each one; if not, just keep counting.

wordCard.voice: Raga Dhanasri. The raga after Sorath, linked by tradition with contentment and true wealth, which opens with a frightened soul and finds riches in service. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: true wealth. Not what you keep, but what you're held by, and what you give. That's today.
